Questions

Which areas do you service?

All of Central Florida, including Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, Lakeland, Kissimmee, Winter Haven and Ocala. If you are just outside those lines, call us and we will tell you honestly whether a route reaches you.

How does valet trash pickup work?

Residents leave a tied bag in the provided container outside their door during the evening window. A uniformed technician collects it and walks it to your compactor or dumpster. Nothing sits out overnight.

How often are pet waste stations serviced?

Once per week or twice per week suits most communities. Larger properties and dog parks often run three visits or a nightly rotation during season.

Do you supply the waste bags?

Yes. Every station is restocked with fresh rolls on every visit at no extra charge, and we clear and wipe down the station area while we are there.

Do you install the stations?

Yes. We install the Doggy Duty pedal dispenser with glow signage, position it where residents actually walk, and the station body carries a lifetime warranty.

What happens if a visit is missed?

We return within 24 hours and credit the visit. If we miss more than two scheduled visits in a month, that month is free. That promise is written into the agreement.

How long is the agreement?

Standard agreements run twelve months and can be cancelled with 30 days written notice. Seasonal terms and short trials are available for boards that want proof first.

Are you licensed and insured?

Yes. Doggy Duty, LLC is licensed and insured, and we send a certificate of insurance for your board packet before the first visit.

Who do residents contact about service?

Residents can email or call us directly, which keeps the office phone quiet. Your manager still receives the written service log after every route.

assistant_content:
All three files are in place.

**Files created**

- **`styles.css`** — hand written design system: Poppins as the single typeface (no italics, capped at semibold), font sizes snapped to the Tailwind type scale via breakpoints instead of clamp, the fixed 13 step spacing token set, Tailwind radius values with the nested radius formula respected (32px card padding so inner chips are unconstrained), flat backgrounds only, all borders full perimeter, dark bands limited to `#131209` / `#181818`, and every transition on `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)`. Includes full hover, active, focus ring, disabled, skeleton loading, empty and inline error states, plus the glass island nav pill and the mobile overlay.
- **`index.html`** — single page, type A layout: floating pill nav (hamburger morphs to an X, full screen glass overlay with staggered link reveals) → hero with gradient heading text (`#000` → `#666`, capped at 680px with meaningful line breaks) and a realistic "service log" panel as the hero visual → proof stats → the two service offers (valet trash, pet waste stations) → the mandatory dark tagline reveal section → five outcome driven benefits → three step "how it works" → station hardware features (pedal lid, glow signage, rain protection and triple storage, lifetime warranty) → schedule picker with a composed empty state → three testimonials from named Central Florida communities → nine question FAQ → final CTA form with risk reversal → footer with contact, social, and real privacy and terms sections anchored on the same page. Icons come from Phosphor, meta title/description/OG tags, FAQ JSON-LD, inline SVG paw favicon, skip to content link, semantic landmarks, and no hyphens or orphaned words in the copy.
- **`script.js`** — no framework: `IntersectionObserver` scroll reveals (translate plus blur to clear over 800ms), per word tagline activation through a thin trigger band in reading order with staggered easing, nav morph and overlay control with focus trapping and Escape handling, the schedule picker state machine, and client side form validation with inline field errors, a skeleton loading state and a calm inline confirmation. No scroll event listeners anywhere.
